items.description: One column's strategy, set by you instead of routed.

column.description: Column name, exactly as in the data.

strategy.description: The strategy. A column that is not numeric, or that profiling skipped, takes only ``passthrough`` or ``dropped``. ``indicator`` is never declared: ``mnar`` adds the ``<column>_missing`` indicator itself.

constant_fill.description: The fill value of a ``constant`` column, which needs one. Null for every other strategy.

grouping_variable.description: For ``cluster_conditional`` only: the column whose groups the fill is taken within. Null takes it per mixture component instead.

strategies.description: Strategies you set, one entry per column. Null means none.

default_strategy.description: The strategy every unlisted numeric column takes. Unlisted columns that are not numeric stay ``passthrough``. Null routes every unlisted column from its profile.

model_choice.description: The estimator the MICE block trains with. Null lets the Estimator Ladder pick it from the block's nonlinearity. Setting it with no ``mice`` column fails.

exclude_columns.description: Columns to leave out of this and every later phase, added to what the profile already excludes. Null means none.

skip_columns.description: Columns routing leaves as they are: ``passthrough`` with reason ``soft_excluded``, and never a predictor. Null means none.

anyOf.description: Every routing dial, grouped. Null keeps every default.
Dials routing reads for numeric columns. Null keeps every default in this group.

knn_max_rows.description: KNN's Resource Ceiling: most rows a frame may have for a column to take ``knn``. Null means 50000. Constraints: at least 1.

mice_min_rows_per_predictor.description: The Feasibility Floor: fewest non-missing rows per predictor a column needs to take ``mice``. Null means 2. Constraints: at least 0.

mice_max_nearest_features.description: Most predictors the Feasibility Floor counts for ``mice``. Null means 20. Constraints: at least 1.

mice_correlation_threshold.description: Least absolute correlation for a column to count as a predictor in the Signal Score's breadth. Null means 0.1. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.

signal_score_breadth_weight.description: How much the count of predictors may add to the Signal Score. Null means 0.1. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.

signal_score_latent_weight.description: How far mutual information alone can raise the Signal Score. Null means 0.3. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.

signal_score_middle_tier_min.description: Signal Score at or above which a column may take a model (``knn`` first). Must not exceed ``signal_score_top_tier_min``. Null means 0.3. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.

signal_score_top_tier_min.description: Signal Score at or above which a column takes the richest feasible model (``mice`` first). Null means 0.6. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.

bimodal_min_correlated_features.description: Fewest correlated columns a bimodal column needs to try a model instead of ``cluster_conditional``. Null means 3. Constraints: at least 1.

bimodal_correlation_threshold.description: Least absolute correlation for a column to count toward ``bimodal_min_correlated_features``. Null means 0.2. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.

numeric.description: The Feasibility Floor, the Signal Score and the bimodal rules.

thresholds.description: Dials, grouped by what they judge, each with its default and range. Null keeps every default.

output.description: The routing Handle and each column's strategy. ``result.get(name)`` finds one column.

warnings.description: Caveats on this result, most actionable first. Empty when there are none.

fields.description: Always exactly `code`, `message`, `columns`, `param`, `hint`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: A caveat on a successful result: it worked, but read this first. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `code`: The warning's Error Code. Branch on this, not on ``message``.
Position 1, `message`: What happened and what to do, in one or two sentences.
Position 2, `columns`: Columns the warning concerns, or null.
Position 3, `param`: The argument the warning concerns, or null.

omitted.description: One entry per list that was cut, naming the Operation that returns the rest. Empty when nothing was cut.

fields.description: Always exactly `field`, `shown`, `total`, `operation`, `reason`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: Something left out of a result: a capped list was cut, or a Literal Field withheld. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `field`: Name of the list field that was cut, or the path of the Literal Field withheld, such as ``top_values[].value``.
Position 1, `shown`: How many items the list holds; 0 for a withheld Literal Field or cut cells.
Position 2, `total`: How many items exist; for a withheld Literal Field, how many values at that path are null; for cut cells, how many were cut.
Position 3, `operation`: The Operation that returns the rest, or null when no Operation does.
Position 4, `reason`: ``cap`` when a list was cut to its cap; ``literal_policy`` when the Operator's Literal Policy is ``deny``; ``truncated`` when long text cells were cut to their character cap.

routing.description: Routing Handle, such as ``routing_7f3a9c2e``. It stores every column's Routing Evidence.

profile.description: The profile Handle that was routed.

mice_estimator.description: The estimator the MICE block trains with; null when no column takes ``mice``.

anyOf.description: Why the MICE block trains with its estimator.

source.description: ``argument`` when ``model_choice`` set it, ``ladder`` when the most complex nonlinearity among the block's columns did.

tag.description: The block's most complex nonlinearity tag. The ladder takes ``random_forest_regressor`` for a nonlinear tag, else ``bayesian_ridge``.

estimator_reason.description: Why ``mice_estimator`` was chosen; null when it is null.

census.description: Columns per strategy, over every column, most first.

fields.description: Always exactly `strategy`, `count`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: How many columns take one strategy. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 1, `count`: Number of ``columns`` rows, indicators included, that take it.

columns.description: Every column but the excluded ones: those that fill or drop values first, then ``passthrough``, each group in dataset order. At most 100; past 100, ``omitted`` counts the rest and names ``explain_routing``.

fields.description: Always exactly `column`, `semantic_type`, `strategy`, `reason`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: One column's strategy and the rule that fixed it. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `column`: Column name. A ``<column>_missing`` row is the indicator an ``mnar`` column adds.
Position 1, `semantic_type`: The profile's semantic type; null when profiling skipped the column. An indicator row is ``boolean``.
Position 2, `strategy`: The strategy the column takes.
Position 3, `reason`: The Routing Reason: the one rule that fixed ``strategy``. ``authored`` when you declared it. ``explain_routing`` gives the evidence behind it.
